nodes.description: HOXA13 encodes the most 5' (caudal/distal) homeobox transcription factor of the HOXA cluster. Heterozygous nonsense, frameshift, gross deletion, and homeodomain missense variants cause haploinsufficiency or abolish homeodomain DNA binding, reducing HOXA13 transcriptional activity in developing distal limb buds and caudal urogenital tissues.

evidence.snippet: The mutation converts a highly conserved tryptophan residue in the homeodomain to a stop codon, which truncates 20 amino acids from the protein and likely eliminates or greatly reduces the ability of the protein to bind to DNA.

evidence.reference_title: Novel HOXA13 mutations and the phenotypic spectrum of hand-foot-genital syndrome.

nodes.description: In-frame expansions across any of the three large exon 1 polyalanine tracts of HOXA13 leave steady-state mRNA levels, splicing, and translation efficiency intact while reducing steady-state HOXA13 protein abundance in vivo (likely via protein degradation), producing a loss-of-function phenotype indistinguishable from null alleles; in vitro overexpression studies additionally report cytoplasmic aggregation and mislocalization of polyalanine-expanded HOXA13.

evidence.reference_title: Polyalanine expansion in HOXA13: three new affected families and the molecular consequences in a mouse model.
evidence.snippet: Here we report additional families with expansions in the third repeat of 11 and 12 alanine residues, the latter being the largest expansion reported. We also report a patient with a novel, de novo 8-alanine expansion in the first large repeat. Thus, expansions in all three large HOXA13 polyalanine repeats can cause HFGS.

evidence.reference_title: Polyalanine expansion in HOXA13: three new affected families and the molecular consequences in a mouse model.
evidence.snippet: Mutant mice were indistinguishable from Hoxa13 null mice. Mutant limb buds had normal steady-state Hoxa13 RNA expression, normal mRNA splicing and reduced levels of steady-state protein. In vitro translation efficiency of the HOXA13(ALA28) protein was normal. Thus, loss of function is secondary to a reduction in the in vivo abundance of the expanded protein likely due to degradation.

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation of HOXA13 in a family with hand-foot-genital syndrome and the role of polyalanine expansions in the spectrum of Müllerian fusion anomalies.
evidence.snippet: Wild type HOXA13 and HOXD13 mislocalize when coexpressed with mutant HOXA13 that contains polyalanine expansions in vitro. The presence of additional alanine residues in the polyalanine tracts of HOXA13 has been shown to cause aggregations of both HOXA13 and HOXD13 in the cytoplasm, preventing these transcription factors from entering the nucleus.

nodes.description: Knock-in mouse carrying a 10-alanine expansion in the third polyalanine tract of Hoxa13 (HOXA13(ALA28)); mutant limb buds retain normal Hoxa13 RNA expression, splicing, and translation efficiency but exhibit reduced steady-state HOXA13 protein abundance in vivo and developmental anomalies indistinguishable from Hoxa13 null mice.

evidence.reference_title: Polyalanine expansion in HOXA13: three new affected families and the molecular consequences in a mouse model.
evidence.snippet: To determine the molecular basis for impaired HOXA13 function, we performed homologous recombination in ES cells in mice to expand the size of the third largest polyalanine tract by 10 residues (HOXA13(ALA28)). Mutant mice were indistinguishable from Hoxa13 null mice.
